title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Explainable AI: Applications in IoT Networks
venue: Kasdi Merbah University - Ouargla Master Thesis
tldr: Explores an integrated framework combining Federated Learning with Explainable AI to enhance data privacy and achieve transparency in AI decision-making for IoT networks and medical systems, evaluating CNN architectures across multiple FL strategies.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional AI systems rely on centralized data aggregation, raising privacy, security, and regulatory compliance concerns. Federated Learning addresses these issues but faces challenges in applying interpretability techniques due to decentralized data. There is tension between strong privacy-preserving techniques and the need for human-understandable interpretations.
approach: Deployed CNN architecture in a federated learning environment across multiple FL strategies (FedAvg, FedOpt, FedAdam, FedYogi).
Evaluated across varied data distributions (balanced, random, skewed), synchronization modes (synchronous/asynchronous), and different numbers of clients.
Integrated visual interpretability tools including GradCAM and NormGrad for model explanation.
Assessed performance metrics including computational efficiency, communication cost, message exchanges, training time, and privacy protection.
Analyzed the impact of privacy-preserving noise on model performance and interpretability.
findings: FedAvg showed training accuracy of 0.95 and evaluation accuracy of 0.94 in balanced data distribution.
FedAdam achieved training accuracy of 0.96 and evaluation accuracy of 0.95 with adaptive learning rates.
Synchronous synchronization outperformed asynchronous with 0.94 vs 0.91 accuracy.
Equal data distribution (balanced) performed better than skewed distribution.
GradCAM and NormGrad effectively highlighted key input regions influencing model predictions.
Privacy-preserving noise at 0.1 level maintained 0.92 accuracy while enhancing privacy.
Increased number of clients (2 to 20) improved model performance but increased communication overhead.
Multi-task federated learning showed comparable accuracy to standard FL with better interpretability.

key_equations.explanation: Federated Averaging aggregates local model weights weighted by dataset sizes to form the global model.
Quantifies privacy protection level by measuring gradient norm reduction after noise addition.

definitions.definition: A decentralized machine learning technique that enables multiple devices to train a shared model without exchanging raw data, sharing only parameter updates.
Techniques that make AI model decisions more transparent and understandable, allowing users to validate predictions and understand reasoning.
Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping, a visualization technique that highlights important regions in input images that influenced model predictions.
A visualization method that computes the norm of gradients to identify significant input features contributing to model output.
A privacy-preserving technique that adds calibrated noise to model updates to prevent leakage of individual data points.
Federated Averaging algorithm that aggregates local model updates from multiple clients to create an improved global model.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This thesis contributes an integrated framework combining Federated Learning with Explainable AI for IoT networks and medical systems. The key innovations include: (1) systematic evaluation of four FL strategies (FedAvg, FedOpt, FedAdam, FedYogi) across different data distributions, (2) integration of GradCAM and NormGrad for visual interpretability in federated settings, (3) analysis of privacy-utility trade-offs with noise injection, and (4) demonstration that synchronous FL with balanced data distribution achieves optimal performance (0.94-0.95 accuracy). The framework addresses the fundamental tension between privacy preservation and model interpretability.
directly_justifies: FedAvg achieved 0.95 training accuracy with balanced data distribution.
Synchronous FL outperformed asynchronous with 0.94 vs 0.91 accuracy.
Privacy noise at 0.1 level maintained 0.92 accuracy while enhancing privacy.
GradCAM and NormGrad effectively highlighted key input regions for model explanation.
Multi-task FL showed comparable accuracy to standard FL with better interpretability.
limits: Master's thesis level research may lack the depth and rigor of journal publications.
Experimental evaluation limited to CNN architecture on specific datasets.
Communication overhead increases significantly with more clients (2 to 20).
Privacy-utility trade-off remains challenging when strong noise is applied.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domains 9.A and 9.B received high relevance as the core focus is on privacy-preserving techniques and regulatory compliance. Domain 12.A received high relevance for comprehensive evaluation frameworks. Domains 6.A and 8.A received medium relevance as the framework can be applied to financial and anomaly detection use cases. Other domains were considered but rejected as the thesis focuses on IoT/medical applications rather than personal finance management.
